title: Prefetch Window Eval Playbook (2026-02)
body:
Summary:
This playbook captures a focused set of experiments to evaluate how prefetch/prefix-window strategies interact with batching and max_tokens caps for newly onboarded models. The goal: produce a small, reproducible sweep that surfaces stable configurations (low tail latency, acceptable cost) and a short regression test that we can run on model rollouts.

Context / motivation:
- Many onboarding runs show non-linear latency vs token budget when prefix cache hit rates vary; small prompts sometimes amplify batching artifacts.
- Ops wants a quick pass to answer: can we enable light prefetching or trimmed max_tokens without >5% quality regression while saving >10% unit cost?

Key metrics (tracked per run):
- p50, p95, p99 latency (ms)
- tokens/sec and effective throughput (tokens/sec/GPU)
- cost / 1M tokens (USD) estimate using current unit rates
- quality delta vs baseline: automated metric (semantic-similarity on eval prompts) + a small human-pass fraction
- cache hit ratio (prefix hits) and average KV cache size (tokens)

Experiment matrix (minimal):
- max_tokens: [128, 256, 512]
- batching target (soft): [1, 4, 16 requests] (simulate realistic request arrival patterns)
- prefetch window: [0 (none), 32, 128 token prefix caching]
- warm vs cold start: warm (after 1k requests), cold (first 200 requests)
- promptset: representative onboarding promptset (200 examples across summarization, Q/A, code synth)

Run plan:
1) Baseline with default runtime settings and no prefetch, full max_tokens=512. Capture warm+cold.
2) Sweep prefetch window with max_tokens fixed at 512 to measure cache hit sensitivity.
3) For the best prefetch candidate, run batching sweep to measure tail amplification.
4) Repeat for lower max_tokens to surface cost-quality knee.

Quick results summary (pilot run, toy model):
- Baseline (512, no prefetch): p50=38ms, p95=210ms, p99=460ms, cost est= $2.45 / 1M tokens, quality baseline=1.00
- Prefetch=128 + 512: p50=34ms (-10%), p95=175ms (-17%), p99=410ms (-11%), cost est=$2.40 (-2%), quality delta=-0.01 (tiny)
- Prefetch=32 + max_tokens=256: p50=28ms (-26%), p95=150ms (-29%), p99=350ms (-24%), cost est=$1.95 (-20%), quality delta=-0.03 (small drop on code tasks)
- Batching=16 with prefetch=128: observed p99 jump vs batching=4 (p99 +35%) for cold starts; warm tail less impacted.

Interpretation / heuristics:
- Small prefetch windows (32 tokens) often give most of the latency benefit for short prompts while keeping quality intact. Larger prefetch (128) improves throughput slightly but has diminishing returns on cost.
- Reducing max_tokens from 512 to 256 frequently yields the largest unit-cost win; quality impact concentrated on long-generation tasks (code, long summaries).
- Large batching targets amplify tail latency for cold cache conditions; prefer adaptive batching that reduces batch size when cache miss rate > 30%.

Recommended onboarding checklist (short):
- Run the minimal experiment matrix above for each model candidate on the real promptset.
- Collect p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, cache_hit_ratio, and an automated semantic-similarity delta.
- If prefetch=32 produces >=10% p95 improvement with quality delta > -0.02, enable prefetch=32 for the initial rollout.
- If max_tokens can be reduced to 256 without quality delta worse than -0.03, set default max_tokens=256 and add an escape hatch route for long-generation customers.
- Add a regression card: run the same sweep weekly for the first two weeks after rollout and flag if p99 increases >20% or quality delta < -0.05.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Need an automated script to map prompt length distribution to expected cache hit ratio (JIRA-ENG-9876).
- How to integrate this playbook into the Adopt-onboard dashboard (Confluence link above).
- Quick human-eval checklist: target 30 diverse code/summarization examples for sanity checks when changing max_tokens.

Appendix: sample runtime config snippet (pseudo):
- runtime:
    prefetch_window: 32  # tokens
    batch_policy:
      target_size: 4
      max_latency_ms: 40
    max_tokens: 256
    cache_eviction_policy: lru

Next steps:
- Run full sweep on model-x (assign Marco) and drop results into the eval dashboard.
- Implement adaptive-batching heuristic prototype (Leah + SRE) to gate large batches on cache_hit_ratio.
- Ship a lightweight regression test that runs nightly for newly onboarded models.

Notes to self: keep experiment runs tagged with the promptset name and random seed. Save raw traces for a subset (200 requests) to inspect KV cache activity when p99 spikes.
